newsitem.title: UK: Siebe lures profit-takers after strong run.
newsitem.headline: Siebe lures profit-takers after strong run.

text.p: Shares in Siebe Plc were the second biggest percent decliner in the FTSE 100 index by later afternoon on Tuesday as some investors cashed in gains in one of the best performing UK blue chip stocks of 1996, dealers said.
Siebe shares were 33-1/2p or 3.1 percent lower at 10.52-1/2 stg by 1503 GMT, surpassed only by the 3.5 percent drop in Redland Plc.

Market-makers said Siebe's decline reflected profit-taking after the stock's recent sharp gains. Siebe shares rose 132p or 13.9 percent during December and were the tenth best FTSE performer in the year as a whole.
"We have been seeing some sellers coming in to take profits," said a market-maker at one top brokerage. "It just seems that people picked on today to take profits."
Conversely he pointed out a firm performance by conglomerate Hanson Plc, up 1p at 85 against the weak trend in the market overall. Hanson was the worst performing FTSE stock in 1996.
"That is a reasonable move for Hanson and it does suggest that some people have been picking up stocks that performed badly during last year," the market-maker said.
